reason: The Hebrew leaders in this text—Mordecai and Esther—actively work to protect and save the Hebrew people from destruction. Mordecai instructs Esther to petition the king to prevent the genocide, and together they secure the Jews' right to defend themselves. The text explicitly states Mordecai 'seeks good for his people' and speaks 'peace to all his descendants.' The antagonism comes from Haman, who is identified as an Agagite (צֹרֵר הַיְּהוּדִים—'enemy of the Jews'), not a Hebrew leader. The narrative consistently portrays the Hebrew leaders as advocates for their people's survival.
